header: Date: 2026-11-05 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~60 minutes | Attendees: Maya Singh, Jon Park, Aisha Kaur, Leo Ramos
summary: Internal SE enablement covering messaging refresh, competitive positioning vs OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock, and live demo practice focusing on dedicated vs hosted routing. Emphasis on objection handling (latency vs cost, VPC/privacy) and next steps to update collateral and record demo clips.
topics: Competitive differentiators (performance, cost controls, private deployments)
Demo walkthrough: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
Objection handling: latency vs cost tradeoffs, security/SOC2/KMS
questions: How do we succinctly explain Dedicated vs Hosted to procurement?
What is the one-liner to counter 'OpenAI has lower latency'?
Which collateral should we send post-call to prospects evaluating private deployments?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone, welcome, thanks for joining the SE enablement. we'll run 60 minutes, cover messaging, competitive, and then do a demo practice. quick intro 00:10 um I'm Maya from AE org, jon will lead the demo, aisha will moderate role-play, leo from product mktg.
[00:23] Jon: hey team, hey. quick note, transcript may have some errors, i've had the demo cluster prepped — Dedicated pool, hosted api, and a VPC config for the private path.
[01:05] Aisha: goal is to leave with one crisp battlecard and a short recorded clip for field. also want to tighten our canned responses on latency vs cost.
[01:28] Leo: product marketing update — we've added the latency vs cost graphic to the deck but need a clear verbal line: 'we trade small increases in latency for 2x cost savings w/ quantized Dedicated configs' that's just a placeholder. feedback?
[01:45] Maya: yeah i like the direction but needs nuance. customers care about p95 latency and tail latencies, not average. say: 'we give predictable p95 with Dedicated and autoscaling while hosted gives fastest time-to-value'.
[02:10] Jon: can i add: for private deployments, callouts are KMS/HSM support, audit logs, and air-gapped packaging — that addresses compliance objections early.
[02:32] Aisha: yes, and note that enterprise folks will ask about SOC2 and ISO — we should point them to the compliance pack and not get into SOC specifics on first call.
[03:00] Maya: ok let's run a quick role-play — i'll be buyer (platform lead), jon you be se demo, aisha you coach. remember common pushback: 'OpenAI's API is simpler' and 'bedrock is in our aws tenant'.
[03:23] Jon (demo): sure, starting the demo, opening dashboard, selecting model catalog. uh excuse the lag, this is on my laptop. [03:40] Jon: so first, hosted api quickstart, one line of code, SDKs for node/python, streaming responses.
[04:12] Buyer (Maya): seems similar to other vendors; why choose Redwood?
[04:20] Jon: good q — our unique is production-grade runtime + cost controls: batching, kv/prefix caching, quantization profiles and smart routing between hosted/dedicated/private. that means you can start hosted and then move to Dedicated to lock down p95 and costs.
[04:55] Buyer (Maya): okay but OpenAI has strong latency and is widely used.
[05:05] Jon: fair — OpenAI has nice infra; our retort is that we focus on inference serving economics: predictable p95 on Dedicated, routing policies to favor cheaper variants midsized loads, and more control for regulated workloads. mention the fallback model policy — if Dedicated is saturated we auto-route to hosted-compatible variant so app stays up.
[05:35] Aisha (coach): good. note: call out a one-liner for AE: 'Redwood gives you the same fast developer experience but with enterprise controls to cut unit costs and meet compliance'.
[06:02] Leo: add competitive notes — Anthropic we lose on safety narrative sometimes; call out that our evals focus on QoE plus cost, and we can surface regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[06:35] Jon: demo pivot — show Dedicated config, CPU/GPU pools, reserved capacity settings, autoscaling policies. [06:55] Jon: speaking of autoscale, customers ask about cold starts — our autoscale can warm nodes based on predictive traffic.
[07:20] Buyer (Maya): what about data residency?
[07:30] Jon: we support region pinning in hosted, and Private deployments let you run in customer VPC or on-prem; plus audit logs and KMS integrations.
[07:50] Maya: great. moving on, let's practice the procurement question: 'We need pricing numbers for QBR' — what do we send?
[08:00] Jon: send the pricing sheet + unit economics model; also show how batching and caching can reduce per-token cost in 30-40% cases. add case study if available.
[08:28] Aisha: note to field — avoid committing custom SLOs without SE alignment. route to SE for any strict latency SLA requests.
[08:45] Jon: role-play two more objections: private/on-prem complexity; then demo freeze and we do feedback.
[09:02] Buyer: "we can't send data off-prem"
[09:08] Jon: reply: "we have Private deployments — customer-managed VPC or on-prem package; key management via KMS/HSM; you keep control of keys and audit logs. we also offer a private control plane option for regulated industries".
[09:40] Aisha: good, call out the compliance pack again.
[09:50] Jon: next objection: "we're worried about model regression after quantization" — our answer: we recommend per-workload evals and Redwood Optimize gives quantization suggestions plus quality monitoring with regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[10:18] Maya: excellent — feedback: be concise on regression: "We run workload-aware evals and gate quantization rollouts with Canary tests to maintain quality".
[10:40] Jon: demo practice — show the routing policy UI: latency-first vs cost-first policies, with automatic fallback thresholds. [11:00] Jon: small transcription note — sometimes UI labels read as 'route rules' in recording.
[11:25] Aisha: ok let's pause — quick lightning feedback from everyone: one thing we liked, one improvement.
[11:40] Maya: liked the latency vs cost graphic, improvement: tighten the Hosted vs Dedicated one-liner.
[11:50] Jon: liked the routing demo, improvement: cut the extraneous infra detail for initial discovery calls.
[12:10] Leo: liked the regression message, improvement: need a 30-second pitch for procurement that summarizes pricing and reserved capacity.
[12:30] Aisha: great. now second half we record a short demo clip — jon, are you comfortable doing a 6-minute clip where you show the model catalog -> configure Dedicated pool -> show routing policy -> show fallback?
[12:44] Jon: yes, i'll do it; i'll mute the mic while i record and then we'll review.
[13:02] [Recording section — demo steps narrated; recording artifacts referenced: link to demo recording omitted in transcript]
[35:00] [Demo recording done — playback review] Jon: playback had a small audio glitch around the autoscale slide, i'll re-record that 30s section.
[35:25] Aisha: feedback on delivery: slower pace, avoid jargon early — e.g., don't say 'KV cache' without first explaining prefix caching.
[36:02] Maya: role-play r2: i'll be procurement this time. ask me about commitment terms.
[36:20] Jon: procurement, our Dedicated reserved capacity comes with monthly/annual commits, flexible burst capacity options, and SLA-backed latency targets; pricing sheet will show commit tiers.
[36:45] Buyer (Maya): can you lower the penalty for underutilization?
[36:52] Jon: we can propose a bilateral flex clause for pilot customers — that's a commercial/AM conversation, escalate to sales ops. don't promise in-call.
[37:10] Aisha: good coach note: always escalate pricing refinements.
[37:22] Leo: quick question — what's our one-liner on model catalog differentiation vs Bedrock?
[37:30] Maya: say: 'we curate open models and verify performance profiles, plus we recommend quantization and kernel profiles for cost/latency tradeoffs' — simple.
[37:50] Jon: caveat: be careful with 'verify' wording; say 'Redwood-verified performance profiles' which is our marketing phrase.
[38:10] Aisha: ok let's finalize action items and next steps.
[38:25] Maya: recap: Maya will update deck, Jon will re-record autoscale snippet and full 6-min clip, Aisha will schedule role-plays. send the compliance pack and pricing spreadsheet to field.
[38:45] Jon: i'll drop the demo clip and upload to the enablement folder, plus add timestamps for key sections.
[39:00] Leo: i'll update the battlecard draft and include the latency vs cost graphic and one-liners.
[39:20] Maya: any final q's?
[39:30] Aisha: none here. thanks team, great session. end.

Notes: transcription contains some mis-hearings of product names (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed 'K V cache'), speaker labels approximate. Links referenced: compliance pack (internal link), pricing spreadsheet (internal link), demo recordings (internal link).
